problem_type: Consecutive creation visibility and acceptance geometry contract drift
symptom: 1280×933 group-baseline first-card click intercepted by rail; batch walk waits for retired progress toast.
direct_cause: Single-card reveal forgets previous creations; launcher has no content-size contract; notification assertions still require removed progress/success alerts.
class_root: Automatic creation viewport lacks a sequence visibility invariant and acceptance does not bind real geometry/current feedback lifecycle.
affected_population: All interactive sequential creation callers in narrow canvas stages
Electron acceptance callers on Linux/macOS with different display sizes

external_sources.purpose: Reuse bounded fit with pixel padding
Minimal offscreen selection pan and bounded zoomToBounds

invariants: Consecutive new cards remain in measured stage until their union cannot fit at the existing minimum zoom.
Existing zoom is retained when sequence fits; only minimum translation is applied.
Stale nodes from deletion/loading and user-directed viewports do not remain in a creation sequence.
Acceptance uses a measured content viewport; notification lifecycle assertions track real nodes and silence probes.
generality_proof: All node additions pass the same nodes-diff hook regardless of caller or media kind; dimensions come from the shared visual-size resolver and actual stage. Electron callers share one launcher dimension assertion.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Track creation sequence and perform bounded minimal reveal using current measured geometry.
Fix and verify content viewport before caller actions.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Toolbar and duplicate additions are observed as node ID additions at the same host hook.
Initial/multi-node snapshots retain existing auto-fit ownership; sequence is reset on non-single additions.
Node status and same DOM replace retired progress/success toast assertions; failure retry remains.

recurrence.reason: Every narrow viewport and future sequential creation can lose previous cards; CI dimensions vary by launcher/display.
same_class_scan: rg useCreatedNodeVisibilityPan and readLastAutoTarget: all automatic reveal callers converge in ReactFlow host.
rg addNode/duplicate in generationCanvas: toolbars, duplication and gradual creation change shared nodes.
rg minZoom/0.2 in generationCanvas: existing fit and gesture lower bound consolidated.
Read _launchApp, journeyRunner, group-baseline and batch-production: launcher dimension and toast policy drift.

prevention.invariant: Retain sequence union in measured stage while readable; then minimally reveal latest at minimum zoom.
prevention.failure_mode: Unmeasured stages do not animate; deleted/replaced snapshots cancel pending sequence; invalid launcher geometry throws rather than silently clamping.
prevention.strategy: Track sequence at shared nodes-diff boundary, reuse React Flow fit and canonical visual geometry; fix viewport at shared launcher.

legacy_paths.rationale: Replace single-last-card-only reveal and retired toast lifecycle assertions in place, no parallel viewport or notification implementation.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Installed React Flow already supplies fit with padding; Playwright click semantics require product geometry correctness, not a dependency workaround.
dependency_lifecycle.target: Current supported installed dependencies; no upgrade required for this invariant.
exit_criteria: Re-evaluate when upstream getViewportForBounds or click geometry changes; sequence and two-size real Electron regressions must remain green.

migration: No persistent data changes. Sequence is ephemeral; existing nodes load via current auto-fit. Acceptance replaces obsolete notification expectations.
residual_risks: Native Linux rerun awaits PR CI; source CI red screenshot and local matching Chromium content geometry are preserved. At the existing minimum zoom a sequence larger than the stage intentionally prioritizes the latest card.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Viewport reveal observes all creation callers and measured stage before any automatic animation; testing only click points cannot prevent user-visible displacement.
